summary: Dash cams are bought first by how many cameras record (front-only, front and rear, plus cabin, or four), then by a price tier and whether the car must be watched while parked; 4K versus 2K front video, 4G remote viewing and special cameras (infrared cabin, waterproof rear, telephoto) split the rest. In the last 60 days DDPAI launched the Z100 Master (3 Nov 2026), a 4K wide plus 2K telephoto front unit at $349 that undercuts VIOFO's A329T at $449.99, and Wolfbox opened a Kickstarter for a 4-camera mirror cam that ships in spring 2027. Prices read on 27 Nov 2026 put Miofive's dual-4K S1 Ultra at $107.99 and Redtiger's F77 at $189.99, both below the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K + 4K at $239.99, while Vantrue's prices are unchanged from 21 Nov.

Our one page built on a bare channel count drew 13 visits against 1.94 site-wide for numbered pages.

Adds a cabin camera (rideshare) or, on VIOFO's A329T, a telephoto; on the VIOFO A329S the front drops from 4K 60 fps to 4K 30 fps with three cameras.

axes.label: recording while the car is parked, and what that needs
axes.why: ChatGPT raised parked recording in all 6 chats; 'best dash cam with parking mode' is Google's first completion of 'best dash cam with'; DashCamTalk lists each pick's parking mode type and says buffered, low-power, radar or energy-saving modes matter more if the vehicle sits unattended.

breakpoints.why: Parking mode needs constant power, and the kit is usually extra: Vantrue's listing says the cam should be hardwired to use parking mode, kit sold separately; DDPAI charges $10 more for the hardwire-kit variant; Miofive's kit is $29.99.
Buffered modes keep the seconds before the trigger. DashCamTalk marks the 70mai T800 'Non-Buffered' and most other picks 'Buffered'.
VIOFO's low-power impact detection on the A329S draws under 40 mA at 12.6 V and wakes in under 2 seconds (VIOFO's figures), which it says turns hours of parked coverage into days.

Radar wakes the camera before impact at low standby draw. DashCamTalk lists the Thinkware U3000 Pro as 'Buffered, Radar'; DDPAI sells radar-accessory variants (N5 Pro Dual + radar, OBD and hardwire kit, $209).

axes.label: supercapacitor instead of a battery
axes.why: 'best dash cam with super capacitor' is a Google completion; DashCamTalk: capacitor-based cameras are usually better suited to hot parked cars and long-term reliability. Most cams in the field have one, so it rarely decides a pick.

breakpoints.why: Maker operating range of -20 to 70 C on Botslab's G980H and Miofive's S1 Ultra; DashCamTalk notes the 70mai M310 Plus 4K has an internal battery and that the A810S replaced its battery with a capacitor.

axes.label: where on the windshield the law lets it sit
axes.why: A legal limit, not a reviewer figure: California Vehicle Code 26708(b)(13) fixes where a video event recorder may be mounted. No line is drawn from it here because no product dimensions were gathered.

breakpoints.why: California allows a recorder in a five-inch square in the lower corner nearest the driver, or in a five-inch square at the center top of the windshield.
California allows a seven-inch square in the lower corner farthest from the driver.

rules: Channels means cameras recording at once, and every resolution or frame rate is stated for that mode: Vantrue's OnDash N4 is 4K only with the front camera alone and 1440p with three cameras, and VIOFO's A329S is 4K 60 fps with two cameras but 4K 30 fps with three. Labels are not comparable across makers. 2K is 2560 x 1440; Vantrue uses both 2.5K and 2.7K for 1944p fronts and 2.5K for a 1440p rear; DDPAI's 3K and Rove's own '4K Upscaled' are not 4K. A 4K claim is read with its sensor, since DashCamTalk separates Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678 cameras from GalaxyCore ones. Prices are for the exact variant: a store's search price is its cheapest variant, 4G and radar are variants on DDPAI, and parking mode needs a hardwire kit that is usually extra (DDPAI +$10, Miofive $29.99), while Redtiger and Botslab bundle cards or kits. A parking claim counts only with the mode named (buffered, low-power draw in mA, radar) and whose figure it is. A 4G comparison includes the data plan. DashCamTalk's scores and its forum measurements (EricSan, TonyM, rcg530) are the named figures for bitrate and frame rate; maker bitrates are not.
